notes: Company background: Mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B) with a heavy in-app assistant and search that surfaces docs + product recommendations.
Current setup: Running prod features on VendorX (OpenAI compatible stack). Considering Redwood to reduce per-token cost and gain routing / dedicated capacity for peak analysis windows.
Primary drivers: cost predictability during monthly reporting windows, lower tail latency for in-app chat, and stronger observability for model regressions tied to product metrics.
Decision team: Head of Product (Maya Chen), Platform Eng lead (Ravi Patel), ML infra (Laura Gomez), Procurement (Michael Ortiz). AE/owner Sofia managing the commercial thread.
Security & compliance: Require SSO (SAML), audit logs for each request, KMS for keying, and ability to confirm EU data residency for a subset of customers.

Technical constraints noted in kickoff: heavy prompt templating across 12 features, reliance on exact prompt-response parity for deterministic UI flows, existing caching layer that assumes OpenAI-compatible KV patterns.
What they like about Redwood so far: unified runtime (hosted -> dedicated), model catalog with perf profiles, routing/fallback ideas could reduce incidents during vendor outages.
POC scope (agreed 2026-02-18):
- Phase A (Hosted): replicate 6 representative prompts in staging, run 72-hour traffic replay (~100k tokens/day), measure latency P50/P95 and generate token-cost comparison versus VendorX.
- Phase B (Parity): evaluate prompt parity/regression via exact-match and semantic checks on 1k golden prompts; flag drift >5% for review.
- Phase C (Dedicated sizing): workshop to map current peak-throughput to Dedicated pool config and estimate reserved capacity commit.

POC findings (technical):
- Latency: Hosted P50 within target (80ms), P95 spikes during replay due to batching heuristics — can be tuned via batching/window config.
- Cost: Projected 15-22% token cost savings on average; potential additional savings with Optimize suggestions (quantization/adaptive batching) if moved to Dedicated.

- Prompt parity: Small but non-trivial regression set. Likely causes: model variant differences, decoding defaults, and prompt-compat shim mismatches. SE recommended two mitigations: prompt normalization layer + controlled decoding params via Redwood API.
- KV cache concerns: Current in-house cache expects exact byte-for-byte match for prefix keys. Need Redwood docs on prefix/KV cache semantics to integrate with Dedicated plan.
